commonMistakes: Boyle’s law requires constant temperature and a fixed amount of gas.
Inverse proportion means doubling volume halves pressure, not doubles it.
Use compatible pressure and volume units on both sides of p₁V₁ = p₂V₂.
A partly correct response can still miss a required unit, relationship, control variable or explanation link.
detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.
Gas pressure is caused by particles colliding with the walls of their container and exerting forces on them. Pressure depends on how frequently and how strongly particles collide with the walls.
For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume. This can be written pV = constant, or p₁V₁ = p₂V₂.
If the volume is reduced while temperature stays constant, particles travel a shorter distance between wall collisions, so collision frequency increases and pressure rises.
In a pressure–volume experiment, temperature should be kept as constant as possible. Compressing a gas too quickly can temporarily heat it, which would confound the intended Boyle’s-law relationship.
examTips: In explanation questions, connect smaller volume to more frequent wall collisions, then to greater force per unit area.
